blinding_guess.why: The declared interface is self-consistent (action and topic names/types match the imports), but on_goal preempts with point0 = sample_traj(self.traj, now) using absolute time.time() instead of now - self.traj_t0 (driver.py:758-759; on_cancel and _update use the relative time), so a goal that preempts a running trajectory starts from the old trajectory's end point; the server also rejects any goal whose points lack velocities (driver.py:735-738) although JointTrajectoryPoint.msg says velocities are optional. The first is a behavioural bug in follow_joint_trajectory; the second may be deliberate.

notes: ROS 1 (hydro): all QoS fields null. definition_id for the action is sha256_normalised of the .action text because definition_hash.py's ros1 mode only hashes .msg files; no ROS 1 md5 of the generated action messages was computed. Dependency definitions fetched from the last hydro release tags: common_msgs 1.10.6 (JointState/JointTrajectory identical at 1.10.0 and 1.10.3; JointTrajectoryPoint identical at 1.10.1-1.10.6, but 1.10.0 lacks the effort field, which would change its md5 and that of JointTrajectory), std_msgs 0.5.8 (Header differs only in comments at 0.5.9), control_msgs 1.2.0 (identical at 1.1.6; 1.3.0 adds error_string). Fetched files were stored in the session scratchpad with a one-line package.xml per package so definition_hash.py can resolve package names; nothing else was fetched. rate_hz null: joint_states is published once per real-time packet from port 30003 (comment '#125 Hz', driver.py:40), no rate is set in code; the follower's internal servo timer is RATE = 0.02 s (driver.py:659, 678) and is not a port rate. rospy.Publisher is created without queue_size (hydro synchronous publish). The action server is created with auto_start=False and started only after the robot connects (driver.py:1003-1004). joint_names accepted by the action are rospy param '~prefix' (default '') + JOINT_NAMES (driver.py:82-83, 903-906), compared as a set (order-independent, then reordered); JointState.name uses the same list. Goals are also rejected if any position/velocity is inf/NaN or any |velocity| > ~max_velocity (default 10.0 rad/s). Goal success requires position within 0.1 and velocity within 0.05 of the last point; timeout abort is commented out (driver.py:838-843), so an unreached goal is never aborted. Other references not in the packet: param robot_description, ~prefix, ~max_velocity, ~min_payload, ~max_payload, prevent_programming, use_sim_time; also publishes wrench (geometry_msgs/WrenchStamped) and io_states (ur_msgs/IOStates) and provides services ur_driver/setPayload and set_io. exclusive: the reverse_port TCP listen socket is bound exclusively; the driver also takes over the robot controller by sending its URScript program to port 30002 (not listed as a code-named resource token).
